key_insight: A projectability-guided AO Hamiltonian construction can transfer plane-wave DFT results, including nonlocal effects, into compact targets suitable for deep-learning Hamiltonian models.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster, more transferable electronic-structure prediction by bridging accurate plane-wave reference calculations with compact atomic-orbital neural-network representations.
method: Select a small set of high-projectability PW eigenstates to define the AO subspace.
Add a few higher-energy states to complete the basis without using an empirical energy shift.
Use PW eigenvalues/eigenstates to implicitly retain nonlocal operator effects for learning PBE and HSE Hamiltonians.
evidence_signal: Benchmarks on MoS2 and sodium phases show that the reconstructed Hamiltonians reproduce PW band structures accurately with smaller AO bases than real-space reconstruction.
watch_item: The approach depends on careful state selection and basis construction, so poor projectability screening could degrade transferability or training quality.
paper_title: Accurately Generalizing Deep-Learning Hamiltonian Methods to Plane-Wave Density Functional Theory
